title: Request Mapping Annotations
description: Learn @RequestMapping, @GetMapping, @PostMapping, and how to define endpoints.

slides.title: The @RequestMapping Family 🏷️
slides.content:
# Shortcuts for Common HTTP Methods

Spring provides annotations to map HTTP requests to controller methods:

* `@GetMapping` – maps GET requests.
* `@PostMapping` – maps POST requests.
* `@PutMapping` – maps PUT requests.
* `@DeleteMapping` – maps DELETE requests.
* `@PatchMapping` – maps PATCH requests.

These are **composed annotations** of `@RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.GET)` etc., making the code more readable.

quizData.question: Which annotation would you use to handle an HTTP PUT request?
quizData.explanation: @PutMapping is the shortcut for handling PUT requests.

slides.title: Advanced Mapping Options
slides.content:
# Narrowing Down Requests

You can also specify:
* `consumes` – what content type the method accepts (e.g., `consumes = "application/json"`).
* `produces` – what content type the method returns (e.g., `produces = "application/xml"`).

If a client sends an unsupported content type, Spring responds with HTTP 415 (Unsupported Media Type).

slides.title: Keep It Consistent 📏
slides.content: Use plural nouns for collections (`/products`) and singular for individual items (`/products/{id}`). This makes your API intuitive.
